Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. Your donations are facilitating Palestinians going to work in Gaza. The transport initiative provides agency and mobility to people, which is crucial during these times. The Sameer Project provides 9 buses daily and transports on average 1,500 people everyday. The buses connect North Gaza with Gaza City and Gaza City with South Gaza. It is important to understand that many vehicles in Gaza have been bombed and the ones still running are barely functioning. No spare parts are allowed into Gaza and the buses we run are constantly breaking down. So having access to transport is huge for Palestinians in Gaza. Support this initiative through the General Fund.

There is something deeply heartbreaking about a little girl in Gaza who has already learned to carry responsibilities that most adults would struggle with, yet still finds the innocence to smile when someone points a camera at her. For a brief moment, she forgets what she’s carrying. She’s just a little girl, happy to be noticed, perhaps excited to see herself on someone’s phone. The kind of ordinary, beautiful reaction you would expect from any child her age. But then you remember where she is. You remember that while children elsewhere are choosing which toys to play with, she is navigating a world where even the simplest necessities require effort, patience, and strength. I wonder what her life would look like if she had been born into peace. What her mornings would sound like. What games she would play. What little things would make her laugh until her stomach hurt. And I hope that one day, she gets to discover all of it. Because the most beautiful thing about her smile isn’t how much suffering she can endure. It’s the little girl who is still there, waiting for a world that will finally let her enjoy being a child. 🇵🇸❤️ #palestine #gaza #fyp #freepalestine #humanity

Palestine’s olive harvest is a tradition passed down through generations, rooted in thousands of years of history. Our olive trees are more than a source of food and livelihood. They are symbols of our identity, our connection to the land, and our steadfastness. Every harvest brings families and communities together to pick olives, share breakfast, and celebrate traditions our ancestors practiced long before us. On October 8, our team gathered with children from the Refaat Alareer Camp on agricultural land in Nuseirat to continue this cherished Palestinian tradition. Despite three years of genocide, displacement, and destruction, our people continue to preserve what the occupation has tried to erase. Our roots run deep. Our traditions endure. Our land is our identity. Help The Sameer Project stand with Palestinians in Gaza and support our General Fund.
